title: Risk Occurrence
rationale: Retain the actuality boundary. Riskium requires an actual occurrence supported in context; a source entry permitting a potential event does not establish realization.
boundary: A scenario alone is not evidence that its occurrence happened.

title: Risk Source
rationale: Retain a bounded analogy. Riskium allows heterogeneous contextual contributors and opportunity perspectives; the security-specific source does not supply that whole cross-category profile.
boundary: Do not assign one universal stereotype or a formal subsumption from a matching label.

title: Predisposing Condition
rationale: Retain the comparison with an explicit direction boundary. The authored Riskium situation increases susceptibility, whereas the inspected source allows likelihood changes in either direction.
boundary: The comparison does not establish a causal mechanism or justify silently broadening the authored definition.

title: Trigger
rationale: Retain the actuality and initiation boundary. A Riskium Trigger is actual and initiating in its context; the compared potential-event entry alone supplies neither commitment.
boundary: A hypothetical trigger remains scenario content.

title: Consequence
rationale: Replace the scoped absence label with a positive comparison boundary: Riskium Consequence is an objective-relevant outcome referent, distinct from the compared potential event. No universal absence claim is made.
boundary: An outcome must not be identified with an event description merely because both occur in a source record.

title: Vulnerability
rationale: Retain the security comparison and identify Mode separately as a modeling foundation. The current intrinsic-susceptibility interpretation requires a supported bearer; exactly-one characterization is distinct from a documentary weakness report.
boundary: Neither shared terminology nor the type annotation supplies actual bearer evidence or independent semantic acceptance.

title: Exposure
rationale: Retain the bounded exposure analogy. The authored Riskium referent is a time-qualified bearer/source situation; the inspected security discussion does not itself define that formal situation model.
boundary: An exposure value is information about the situation, not the situation itself.

title: Risk State
rationale: Replace the scoped absence label with a contrast. Riskium explicitly individuates a temporally qualified risk situation; generic entity description does not supply its state identity or a workflow interpretation.
boundary: A record workflow status must not be substituted for the state of the risk-relevant situation.

title: Information Content
rationale: Retain conceptual-entity context without importing a content identity policy. Riskium keeps abstract meaning separate from artifacts and versions and requires its own explicit equivalence criteria.
boundary: Equal strings or file digests alone do not establish content identity.

title: Entry Revision
rationale: Retain the object/derivation distinction. Riskium EntryRevision is a version object with effective links; a qualified revision describes derivation rather than being that version or its creation activity.
boundary: Do not substitute a derivation qualification for an entry-version individual.

title: Assessment Activity
rationale: Retain the activity/process scope distinction. A Riskium AssessmentActivity may contribute only one actual part of identification, analysis or evaluation; it is not automatically the complete security assessment process.
boundary: A planned assessment is not an actual assessment activity.

title: Treatment Activity
rationale: Retain the response analogy and separate actual treatment performance from its plan. Intended risk modification does not by itself establish observed effectiveness.
boundary: A documented plan alone does not establish an executed treatment.

title: Risk Control
rationale: Retain the security-control analogy as one contextual use of Riskium RiskControl. The authored profile permits different bearer categories and separates implementation from effectiveness.
boundary: A named or installed measure alone is not proof of effectiveness; no cross-category stereotype is forced.

title: Responsibility Relator
rationale: Retain Relator as a modeling foundation rather than an external responsibility definition. Riskium adds grounding, temporal scope and responsibility semantics; its distinct-participant identity rule is additional to the C2 minimum-cardinality sum.
boundary: An owner name alone does not establish a grounded mandate or distinct mediated participants; independent judgment remains #23.

title: Workflow Scheme Version
rationale: Retain the comparison boundary. Riskium WorkflowSchemeVersion is an issued transition specification; concept-scheme aggregation or a revision qualification does not define its transitions or authorization rules.
boundary: Do not infer executable workflow rules from a concept aggregation or version lineage.

title: Workflow Assignment
rationale: Replace the scoped absence label with a contrast. Riskium WorkflowAssignment is a timed record-state situation under a scheme version, rather than an activity-function description.
boundary: The statement documenting an assignment is distinct from the assignment situation.

title: Observation Activity
rationale: Retain the procedure/feature/value observation comparison. Riskium keeps its stated subject, procedure and temporal context without automatically importing every source restriction.
boundary: An observation report is information about an activity; the comparison does not establish all-profile equivalence.
